source_text:
Εὔοδος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, πρῶτος ἐπίσκοπος

Ἀντιοχείας μετὰ Πέτρον τὸν κορυφαῖον ἐγένετο.
ξʹ. Φιλήμων, πρὸς ὃν ἐπιστολὴν ἰδίαν ὁ Παῦλος ἔγραψεν, ἐπίσκοπος Γάζης
ἐγένετο.
ξαʹ. Ζηνᾶς ὁ νομικός, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος
∆ιοσπόλεως γέγονεν.
ξβʹ. Ἀκύλας, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Ἡρακλείας ἐγένετο.
ξγʹ. Πρίσκας, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Κολοφῶνος
ἐγένετο.
ξδʹ. Ἰουνίας, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Ἀπαμείας τῆς
Συρίας ἐγένετο.
126 ξεʹ. Μάρκος ὁ καὶ Ἰωάννης καλούμενος, οὗ μέμνηται ὁ Λουκᾶς ἐν ταῖς
πράξεσι τῶν ἀποστόλων, ἐπίσκοπος Βίβλου ἐγένετο.
ξς ʹ. Ἀρίσταρχος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται.
ξζʹ. Πούδης, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται.
ξηʹ. Τρόφιμος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος μέμνηται. Οὗτοι οἱ τρεῖς ἐν
πᾶσι τοῖς διωγμοῖς τοῦ ἀποστόλου Παύλου συγκακοπαθήσαντες αὐτῷ, τελευταῖοι
καὶ διὰ μαρτυρίου σὺν ἐκείνῳ ἐτελειώθησαν ὑπὸ Νέρωνος τὰς κεφαλὰς σὺν ἐκείνῳ
ἀποτμηθέντες. Τούτοις συναριθμουμένων καὶ Μάρκου καὶ Λουκᾶ τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ
ὁμοῦ
οʹ. Τοῦ ἁγίου Ἐπιφανίου ἀρχιεπισκόπου Κύπρου.
Ταῦτα τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν ιβʹ ἀποστόλων.
αʹ. Πέτρος, οὗτος ἐλέγετο καὶ Σίμων καὶ Κηφᾶς καὶ Συμεών.
βʹ. Ἀνδρέας ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ.
γʹ. Ἰάκωβος. δʹ. Ἰωάννης, οὗτοι βοανεργὲς ἐκαλοῦντο, ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται υἱοὶ
βροντῆς.
εʹ. Φίλιππος.
ςʹ. Βαρθολομαῖος.
ζʹ. Ματθαῖος ὁ τελώνης.
ηʹ. Θωμᾶς, οὗτος καὶ ∆ίδυμος ἐκαλεῖτο.
θʹ. Ἰάκωβος Ἀλφαίου.
ιʹ. Θαδδαῖος, οὗτος παρὰ μὲν τῷ Ματθαίῳ Λεββαῖος καλεῖται, παρὰ δὲ τῷ
Λουκᾷ Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου, παρὰ δὲ τῷ Μάρκῳ Λευὶς καθήμενος παρὰ τὸ τελώνιον.
ιαʹ. Σίμων ὁ Κανανίτης.
ιβʹ. Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριότης, καὶ ἀντὶ τούτου Ματθίας εἰσῆλθεν Ἀδελφοὶ δὲ
Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας, υἱοὶ Ἀννᾶς, καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης, υἱοὶ Ζεβεδαίου,
Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰούδας, υἱοὶ Ἀλφαίου, ἁλιεῖς. Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας, Ἰάκωβος καὶ
Ἰωάννης. Ἰάκωβος ὁ καλούμενος ἀδελφὸς τοῦ κυρίου, ποῖος ἦν ὁ γενόμενος
ἐπίσκοπος Ἱερουσαλήμ, ὁ ἐπονομαζόμενος δίκαιος, ὁ εἷς ἦν υἱὸς Ζεβεδαίου καὶ ὁ
ἕτερος Ἀλφαίου, καὶ ὁ ἄλλος τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ τοῦ μνήστορος, ὡς ἔλεγον Ἰουδαῖοι.
Σίμωνα καὶ Ἰούδα, Ἰωσὴ τὸν ἀδελφόν, Ματθαῖος λέγει αὐτοὺς καλεῖσθαι τελῶνας,
Λουκᾶς δὲ καὶ Λευῒν κεκλῆσθαι τελῶνα. Ἰωνᾶς δὲ ἑρμηνεύεται περιστερά.
thought_title: End of the seventy and names of the twelve
orientation: Epiphanius finishes listing the seventy disciples and then gives the list of the twelve apostles with notes on their families.
pass_a_gloss: Euodus, whom Paul also mentions, became first bishop of Antioch after Peter the chief. 60. Philemon, to whom Paul wrote a private letter, became bishop of Gaza. 61. Zenas the lawyer, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Diospolis. 62. Aquila, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Heraclea. 63. Priscas, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Colophon. 64. Junias, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Apamea of Syria. 65. Mark who is also called John, whom Luke mentions in the Acts of the Apostles, became bishop of Byblos. 66. Aristarchus, whom Paul also mentions. 67. Pudens, whom Paul also mentions. 68. Trophimus, whom the apostle Paul also mentions. These three, having suffered evil together with him in all the persecutions of the apostle Paul, at last also by martyrdom together with him were perfected under Nero, with heads cut off together with him. With these being counted together also Mark and Luke the evangelist together seventy. By the holy Epiphanius archbishop of Cyprus. These are the names of the twelve apostles. 1. Peter, this one was called both Simon and Cephas and Symeon. 2. Andrew his brother. 3. James. 4. John, these were called Boanerges, which is interpreted sons of thunder. 5. Philip. 6. Bartholomew. 7. Matthew the tax collector. 8. Thomas, this one was also called Didymus. 9. James of Alphaeus. 10. Thaddaeus, this one by Matthew is called Lebbaeus, and by Luke Judas of James, and by Mark Levi sitting by the tax office. 11. Simon the Cananaean. 12. Judas Iscariot, and in place of this one Matthias entered. And brothers were Peter and Andrew, sons of Annas, and James and John, sons of Zebedee, James and Judas, sons of Alphaeus, fishermen. Peter and Andrew, James and John. James the one called brother of the Lord, who was the one who became bishop of Jerusalem, the one surnamed Just, which one was he, the one was son of Zebedee and the other of Alphaeus, and the other of Joseph the betrothed, as Jews were saying. Simon and Judas, Joseph the brother, Matthew says they were called tax collectors, but Luke says also Levi was called tax collector. And Jonah is interpreted dove.

choices.why: brief glossary fixes koruphaios as chief for Peter
brief glossary fixes telones as tax collector
brief glossary fixes this phrase as sons of thunder
brief glossary fixes this phrase as brother of the Lord
literal sense for explanation of names, keeps passive force

pass_b_english: 59. Euodus, whom Paul also mentions, became the first bishop of Antioch after Peter the chief. 60. Philemon, to whom Paul wrote a personal letter, became bishop of Gaza. 61. Zenas the lawyer, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Diospolis. 62. Aquila, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Heraclea. 63. Priscas, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Colophon. 64. Junias, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Apamea in Syria.

65. Mark, also called John, whom Luke mentions in the Acts of the Apostles, became bishop of Byblos. 66. Aristarchus, whom Paul also mentions. 67. Pudens, whom Paul also mentions. 68. Trophimus, whom the apostle Paul also mentions. These three shared all the persecutions of the apostle Paul and suffered with him, and in the end they were perfected with him through martyrdom under Nero, beheaded with him. With Mark and Luke the evangelist counted with them, they come to seventy together.
By Saint Epiphanius, Archbishop of Cyprus. These are the names of the twelve apostles.

1. Peter, who was also called Simon and Cephas and Symeon. 2. Andrew, his brother. 3. James. 4. John. These two were called Boanerges, which is interpreted sons of thunder. 5. Philip. 6. Bartholomew. 7. Matthew the tax collector. 8. Thomas, who was also called Didymus. 9. James son of Alphaeus. 10. Thaddaeus. Matthew calls him Lebbaeus, Luke calls him Judas son of James, and Mark calls him Levi sitting at the tax office. 11. Simon the Cananaean. 12. Judas Iscariot, and Matthias entered in his place.

Peter and Andrew were brothers, the sons of Annas. James and John were the sons of Zebedee. James and Judas were the sons of Alphaeus. The fishermen were Peter and Andrew, James and John. As for James, who is called brother of the Lord, which one was it who became bishop of Jerusalem, called the Just. One James was the son of Zebedee and the other was the son of Alphaeus, and the other was the son of Joseph the betrothed, as the Jews said. Matthew says that Simon and Judas and Joseph the brother were called tax collectors, and Luke says that Levi too was called a tax collector. Jonah is interpreted dove.
notes: The figure 126 before 65 looks like a page or line number, not part of the list; list numbers are glossed as written.

problems.quote: James and Judas were the sons of Alphaeus, and they were fishermen. I mean Peter and Andrew, James and John.
problems.source_quote: Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰούδας, υἱοὶ Ἀλφαίου, ἁλιεῖς. Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας, Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης.
problems.why: Misreads ἁλιεῖς as applying to James and Judas and invents 'I mean'; ἁλιεῖς introduces the fishermen: Peter, Andrew, James, and John.
problems.fix: James and Judas were the sons of Alphaeus. The fishermen were Peter and Andrew, James and John.
problems.ruling: ἁλιεῖς precedes Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας, Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης; English binds ἁλιεῖς to υἱοὶ Ἀλφαίου and adds unstated 'I mean'.

edits.old: James and Judas were the sons of Alphaeus, and they were fishermen. I mean Peter and Andrew, James and John.
edits.new: James and Judas were the sons of Alphaeus. The fishermen were Peter and Andrew, James and John.

fixed: Fixed fishermen clause: source ὁλιεῖς with Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας, Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης identifies Peter, Andrew, James and John as the fishermen, not James and Judas.

last_rejected.source_quote: Τούτοις συναριθμουμένων καὶ Μάρκου καὶ Λουκᾶ τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ ὁμοῦ
last_rejected.why: Source names Mark and Luke counted together but never states the number seventy.
last_rejected.fix: With Mark and Luke the evangelist counted together with them as well.
last_rejected.ruling: Source reads "ὁμοῦ οʹ." across the line break; Greek numeral οʹ is 70 (68 plus Mark and Luke), not an addition.
